ing: optional; or finely chopped green bell pepper
st: Mix [[2 cup]] masa harina with [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Add [[1.5 cup]] warm water a little at a time, kneading until you have a soft dough like play dough.
Rest the dough, covered, for 10 minutes. If it cracks when pressed, knead in a spoonful of water.
Mix the cheese with the loroco if using. Mix the pork with the refried beans if you want a pork and bean filling.
Oil your hands. Roll a ball of dough the size of a lime and press a deep hole into it with your thumb.
Fill with a heaping spoonful of filling, fold the dough up around it and pinch closed.
Pat the ball between your palms into a round disc about 0.25 inch thick. Smooth any cracks.
Heat a griddle or skillet over medium-high heat with a thin film of oil. Cook each pupusa for 4 minutes per side until browned with a few dark spots.
Serve hot with curtido and salsa roja.
Put the shredded cabbage in a large heatproof bowl and pour [[2 cup]] hot water over it. Let it sit for 3 minutes to soften, then drain well.
Add the carrots, onion and jalapeno to the cabbage.
Stir [[1 cup]] vinegar, [[1 tsp]] oregano and [[1 tsp]] salt together, then pour it over the vegetables.
Toss well and press down so the vegetables are covered with liquid.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Overnight is even better.
Drain a little of the liquid before serving cold alongside pupusas or fried foods.
Put the tomatoes, onion, garlic and bell pepper in a pot with [[0.5 cup]] water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 15 minutes until everything is soft.
Let it cool for 5 minutes.
Blend with [[0.5 tsp]] oregano and [[0.75 tsp]] salt until smooth.
Pour back into the pot and simmer for 5 minutes until slightly reduced. The sauce should be thin and pourable.
Taste and adjust salt. Serve warm over pupusas.
Cut the cassava into thick sticks about 3 inches long. Remove any tough woody core.
Boil the cassava in [[8 cup]] water with [[1 tsp]] salt for 20 minutes until just tender. Drain and dry on paper towels.
Toss the cabbage with [[0.25 cup]] vinegar, the lime juice and a pinch of salt. Chill as the slaw.
Mix the tomatoes with a pinch of salt for a quick fresh salsa.

Place the pork belly cubes in a pot with a little water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Simmer for 30 minutes, then let the water boil off so the pork fries in its own fat, about 10 minutes more, until brown and crisp. Pork must reach 145°F (63°C).
Heat [[3 cup]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Fry the cassava in batches for 5 minutes until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Serve the cassava topped with the chicharrón, the slaw and the tomato salsa.
Rinse the cow feet and tripe well. Rub them with half of the lime juice and rinse again.
Put them in a large pot with [[12 cup]] water, the onion and garlic. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Add [[2 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Cover and simmer for 3 hours, until the meat is very tender.
Add the cassava and corn. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the plantains and cabbage. Simmer for 15 minutes more until all the vegetables are tender.
Taste and add salt if needed. Stir in [[0.5 cup]] cilantro.
Ladle into bowls with the meat and vegetables, and squeeze the remaining lime juice into each bowl.
Put the chicken in a pot with [[3 cup]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer for 30 minutes until it reaches 165°F (74°C). Remove and shred, saving the broth.
Toast [[0.25 cup]] pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 3 minutes, then grind them fine.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil. Cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes. Add the tomatoes and [[1 tbsp]] achiote and cook 8 minutes.
Blend the tomato mixture and ground seeds with a cup of the broth until smooth.
Return the sauce to the pan with the shredded chicken and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Split the rolls and warm them in the oven for 5 minutes.
Fill each roll with chicken and sauce, then top with watercress, cucumber and radishes. Serve right away.
Soak the corn husks in warm water for 30 minutes until soft.
Blend the corn with [[0.5 cup]] milk until almost smooth but still a little textured.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[0.25 cup]] melted butter, [[0.25 cup]] cornmeal and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Spread a husk flat and put a heaping spoonful of batter in the center. Fold the sides in, then fold up the bottom.
Stand the tamales open end up in a steamer basket over [[1 cup]] boiling water.
Cover and steam for 60 minutes, adding hot water as needed. A tamale is done when the dough pulls cleanly from the husk.
Rest 10 minutes before unwrapping. Serve warm with sour cream.
Boil the diced potato and carrot in water for 8 minutes until just tender. Drain.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pan. Cook the onion for 3 minutes, then add the beef and cook 8 minutes, breaking it up, until it reaches 160°F (71°C).
Stir in the potato, carrot, [[1 tsp]] achiote and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cool the filling for 15 minutes.
Mix [[2 cup]] masa harina, [[0.75 tsp]] salt and [[1.5 cup]] warm water into a soft dough. Rest 10 minutes.
Roll the dough between plastic sheets to 0.1 inch thick and cut 5 inch circles.
Put a spoonful of filling on half of each circle, fold over, and press the edges with a fork.
Heat [[3 cup]] oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry the pastelitos 3 minutes per side until golden. Drain and serve hot with curtido.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9 inch round or square cake pan.
Cream [[0.5 cup]] butter with [[0.75 cup]] sugar for 3 minutes until fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then mix in [[0.5 cup]] sour cream.
Stir in [[1 cup]] grated cheese and [[0.5 cup]] milk.
Whisk [[2 cup]] rice flour, [[1 tbsp]] baking powder and [[0.25 tsp]] salt, and fold into the batter until smooth.
Pour into the pan, smooth the top and sprinkle with [[2 tbsp]] sesame seeds.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 15 minutes in the pan before slicing. Serve with coffee.
Blend [[3 cup]] corn with [[1 cup]] water until very smooth.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into a pot, pressing out all the liquid. Discard the pulp.
Add the cinnamon stick and [[2 cup]] milk to the pot.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 15 minutes until it thickens like thin pudding.
Stir in [[0.33 cup]] sugar and a pinch of salt. Cook 3 more minutes.
Remove the cinnamon stick and serve warm in mugs, dusted with ground cinnamon.
